headline: Fed interest rate trajectory remains the key near-term inflection point to watch for gold's next move
reasoning: Fan identifies the yield environment and Federal Reserve interest rate policy as still the major near-term variable for the gold price. While the structural demand story from central banks and institutional investors is intact, shifts in Fed policy expectations will likely determine the timing of gold's next significant price move.
quote: Certainly, you know, the the yield environment, especially Fed interest rates are still going to be a major factor.
episode_title: Why investors are buying gold as yields rise

headline: Central bank gold buying remains very strong, with China purchasing 20–30 tonnes per month above historical averages, supporting the broader gold demand narrative
reasoning: Fan notes that central bank physical gold demand continues to be robust based on monthly data. China has been buying between 20 and 30 tonnes per month in recent months, above the historical average. Other central banks are also continuing to buy on the physical front. Fan attended three central bank conferences in 30 days and observed gold is front and centre in virtually every session, reflecting strong enthusiasm among the central bank community. This central bank buying underpins gold's role as a diversifier and hedge against geopolitical and fiscal instability.
quote: Central bank gold demand probably continues to be very strong from the monthly data we've seen. China for instance, has bought gold about between 20 and 30 tonnes per month in the last couple of months, which has been higher than the historical average. And we've continued to see a buying from many other central banks on the physical front too. So there is still that central bank buying supporting the narrative. The ETF buying supports the narrative that investors are continuing to see gold as a diversifier and also as a hedge against instability in the world, instability in fiscal budgets.
episode_title: Why investors are buying gold as yields rise

headline: Rising bond yields driven by fiscal sustainability fears are paradoxically boosting gold ETF inflows globally, with investors treating price weakness as a buying opportunity
reasoning: Despite gold prices falling under pressure from rising US bond yields, investor demand for gold ETFs has remained strong across the US, Europe, UK, Australia, and Asia. Fan argues the primary driver is not yield arithmetic but rather growing concerns about fiscal sustainability and governments' ability to repay debt. He views gold's status as the only major asset class not issued by any government as the core investment thesis. Australia alone saw approximately $100 million USD of inflows into gold ETFs in September. The trend is described as near-universal across developed and emerging markets in Q3.
quote: I think probably the overriding factor is why are bond yields rising, which is, you know, continued worries about fiscal sustainability in many markets, worries about the government's ability to repay debt. And I think that's kind of a long term trend and erosion of trust that's driving the investment case into gold as you know, the only major asset class that's not issued by any government. So across all markets, we're seeing this trend continue and you know, it's been almost universal in Australia, in the UK and the US and Asia. We've seen strong inflows into gold ETFs in Q3 despite the fact that gold prices have been moving lower.
episode_title: Why investors are buying gold as yields rise

headline: Jewellery demand expected to remain weak due to elevated gold prices, consistent with historical patterns
reasoning: Fan flags that jewellery demand for gold has traditionally softened during periods of high gold prices, and he expects this trend to continue in Q3 based on historical evidence, even though the full Q3 picture is not yet available. This represents a soft spot within overall gold demand, contrasting with the strength in ETF and central bank buying.
quote: Where we continue to probably see weaknesses, you know, the other elements of gold demand, jewellery demand for instance, which traditionally has been lower because of higher gold prices. Although we don't have a full picture of what's happening in Q3 for the jewellery market, I think, you know, historical evidence does point to continued weakness in that area because of higher gold prices.

headline: Bullish on gold despite lower prices, as institutional inflows strengthen and the traditional inverse relationship with US rates and the dollar weakens due to structural buyers like Chinese retail and central banks
reasoning: Shaokai Fan notes strong inflows into gold over the last couple of months even as prices have dipped, suggesting investors are actively positioning into gold. He highlights that while Fed interest rates remain a major short-term factor for gold, the long-run relationship between US rates, the US dollar, and gold has weakened. This is because new structural buyers — Chinese retail investors and central banks — have entered the market for reasons unrelated to the US rate cycle. He flags the upcoming Q3 Gold Demand Trends report as a key data point to watch for shifts in physical demand. He also points to new gold trading centres emerging in Singapore and Hong Kong as a sign that Asia-Pacific is becoming the centre of global gold demand.
quote: In the long run, we have seen a weakening of that traditional relationship between US rates and the US dollar and gold because there have been so many other investors who moved into the gold market in the last couple of years, like Chinese retail investors, like central banks, of course, who are buying gold for their own reasons that are often not related to the US rate cycle. So I would look at physical demand and when we release our third quarter gold demand trends report that outlines the entire gold market, that would be a very, you know, important piece of data to look at and see if there are underlying shifts in physical demand. Another major happening in the gold market is of course the development of new gold trading centres in Singapore and Hong Kong and just a sign of the market being much more focused on Asia and Asia Pacific as the centre for gold demand going forward.
episode_title: Why investors are buying gold as yields rise
